an10.2:1.1: (1)–(2) “Bhikkhus, for a virtuous person, one whose behavior is virtuous, no volition need be exerted:
an10.2:1.3: It is natural that non-regret arises in a virtuous person, one whose behavior is virtuous.
an10.2:1.4: (3) “For one without regret no volition need be exerted:
an10.2:1.6: ‘Let joy arise in me.’ It is natural that joy arises in one without regret.
an10.2:1.7: (4) “For one who is joyful no volition need be exerted:
an10.2:1.9: ‘Let rapture arise in me.’ It is natural that rapture arises in one who is joyful. (5)
an10.2:1.10: “For one with a rapturous mind no volition need be exerted:
an10.2:1.12: ‘Let my body be tranquil.’ It is natural that the body of one with a rapturous mind is tranquil.
an10.2:1.13: (6) “For one tranquil in body no volition need be exerted:
an10.2:1.15: It is natural that one tranquil in body feels pleasure.
an10.2:1.16: (7) “For one feeling pleasure no volition need be exerted:
an10.2:1.18: It is natural that the mind of one feeling pleasure is concentrated.
an10.2:1.19: (8) “For one who is concentrated no volition need be exerted:
an10.2:1.20: ‘Let me know and see things as they really are.’
an10.2:1.21: It is natural that one who is concentrated knows and sees things as they really are.
an10.2:1.22: (9) “For one who knows and sees things as they really are no volition need be exerted:
an10.2:1.24: It is natural that one who knows and sees things as they really are is disenchanted and dispassionate.
an10.2:1.25: (10) “For one who is disenchanted and dispassionate no volition need be exerted:
an10.2:1.26: ‘Let me realize the knowledge and vision of liberation.’
an10.2:1.27: It is natural that one who is disenchanted and dispassionate realizes the knowledge and vision of liberation.
an10.2:2.1: “Thus, bhikkhus, (9)–(10) the knowledge and vision of liberation is the purpose and benefit of disenchantment and dispassion;
an10.2:2.2: (8) disenchantment and dispassion are the purpose and benefit of the knowledge and vision of things as they really are;
an10.2:2.3: (7) the knowledge and vision of things as they really are is the purpose and benefit of concentration;
an10.2:2.4: (6) concentration is the purpose and benefit of pleasure;
an10.2:2.5: (5) pleasure is the purpose and benefit of tranquility;
an10.2:2.6: (4) tranquility is the purpose and benefit of rapture;
an10.2:2.7: (3) rapture is the purpose and benefit of joy;
an10.2:2.8: (2) joy is the purpose and benefit of non-regret;
an10.2:2.9: and (1) non-regret is the purpose and benefit of virtuous behavior.
an10.2:2.10: “Thus, bhikkhus, one stage flows into the next stage, one stage fills up the next stage, for going from the near shore to the far shore.”
